Id. at 134.

Furthermore, the Supreme Court has reinforced this principle in "United States v. Johnson," 529 U.S. 53 (2000), where it stated that "[t]he parties must raise their contentions at the earliest practicable moment in the district court, and failure to do so will result in the waiver of those contentions on appeal." Id. at 62.

In fact, the Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure explicitly state that "[a] party waives all issues that the party did not raise in the district court." Fed. R. App. P. 3(a)(1). This is clearly a black-letter rule of law that has been consistently applied in the lower courts.
